evals.prompt: Can you review this class before I merge it? [pastes a 150-line OrderService that validates, prices, saves via JDBC and sends email, using ArrayList and null returns]
evals.expected_output: Request changes; SRP blocker with a concrete split into validator/pricer/repository/notifier/use case; immutability and Option findings grouped; coverage stated as estimated with a hand-built coverage map

evals.prompt: Here's my test class for the pricing module - is it any good? [pastes JUnit 5 tests mixing assertEquals, an assertThat(x) with nothing chained, a test with no assertion, and a try/fail/catch]
evals.expected_output: Blockers for the assertion-less test and the unchained assertThat; AssertJ rewrites of the JUnit assertions; assertThatThrownBy replacing try/fail/catch

evals.prompt: Review the repo I've uploaded (Maven, has target/site/jacoco/jacoco.xml).
evals.expected_output: Runs the scanner with the JaCoCo report, confirms hits by reading code, reports measured coverage per class below 95/90, report in the standard format with grouped findings

evals.prompt:
Review this method: public int score(List<Round> rounds, int bonus) { int total = 0; for (Round r : rounds) { if (r.won()) total += r.points(); } // add the bonus
 return total + bonus; }
evals.expected_output: Major findings: non-final parameters and local; the for and if statements have no justifying comment (and '// add the bonus' is not a justification). Fix: final parameters, rounds.filter(Round::won).map(Round::points).fold(0, Integer::sum) + bonus, no control-flow statements.
